newsitem.title: UK: Buoyant LME copper soars to fresh one-year high.
newsitem.headline: Buoyant LME copper soars to fresh one-year high.

text.p: London Metal Exchange (LME) copper prices rallied more than $50 on Wednesday to the highest in nearly 13 months, helped up by what traders said were positive technicals that encouraged some investor buying.
The day's high of $2,570 was the firmest level since May 17, 1996, although profit-taking took the top off of the rally during the afternoon kerb, dealers said.
Three months metal ended the kerb at $2,561 per tonne, compared to $2,514 on Tuesday.
Copper started chugged higher early in the day on mostly speculative buying, following on Tuesday's constructive close above $2,500.
It continued to snap higher in the morning and afternoon rings after triggering key stops, particularly the $2,550 resistance level, traders said.
"There was no obvious reason for it, but bank buying was driving prices higher today. Although on the other hand there was trade and producer selling," a trader said.
Volumes were not particularly significant, however, traders noted.
A flaring backwardation -cash to threes ended at $105, compared to $63 at the start of the week- was supportive.
Aluminium, boosted by copper's gains and a 4,350-tonne LME stock drop, also made a foray to the upside. But it stalled around $1,630 and settled at the kerb at a $6 firmer $1,623.
Nickel, also with an eye to copper, pushed up nearly $100 to a peak of $7,380 in the first part of the day.
But dealers said the market failed to sustain any upside momentum and fell back. It ended at $7,260, down $30.

"Nickel was pulled up on copper's sentiment, but it got overextended and came off again," a trader said, noting that the market was somewhat long recently because of nervousness over Inco's ongoing Sudbury strike.
Zinc ended $5 higher at $1,368 and appeared to be building a base below the recent 4-1/2 year high of $1,677 before tackling the upside again, analysts said.
Tin finished virtually unchanged at $5,600, off $10, while lead sank $3 to $637. Alloy was quiet and last indicated little changed at $1,486/$1,490.
